ref_atoms.ref_content: Interrupt hmac_done: HMAC/SHA-2 has completed.

Interrupt fifo_empty: The message FIFO is empty. This interrupt is raised only if the message FIFO is actually writable by software, i.e., if all of the following conditions are met: i) The HMAC block is not running in HMAC mode and performing the second round of computing the final hash of the outer key as well as the result of the first round using the inner key. ii) Software has not yet written the Process or Stop command to finish the hashing operation. For the interrupt to be raised, the message FIFO must also have been full previously. Otherwise, the hardware empties the FIFO faster than software can fill it and there is no point in interrupting the software to inform it about the message FIFO being empty.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies conditions for the fifo_empty interrupt including message FIFO writability, HMAC mode round, and not yet written Process/Stop command; Informativeness: describes detailed hardware behavior for interrupt assertion.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Interrupt hmac_err: HMAC error has occurred. ERR_CODE register shows which error occurred.
Alert fatal_fault: This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies the fatal alert triggered by TL-UL bus integrity fault; Informativeness: describes exact trigger condition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Feature HMAC.SECURE_WIPE: Wipe of internal state and secret key with constant value provided by software.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: refers to the wipe operation of internal state and secret key with a constant; Informativeness: describes the mechanism of clearing internal variables.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CFG register: HMAC Configuration register. The register is updated when the engine is in Idle. If the software updates the register while the engine computes the hash, the updated value is discarded. Field hmac_en: If 1, HMAC operates when hash_start toggles. Field sha_en: If 0, the SHA engine will not initiate compression; when the SHA-2 engine is disabled the digest is cleared. Field endian_swap: If 0, each value will be added to the message in little-endian byte order; if 1, then each individual multi-byte value written to MSG_FIFO will be added in big-endian byte order; a message written one byte at a time is unaffected; byte swaps are performed on a TL-UL word granularity. Field digest_swap: If 1, the value in each digest output register is converted to big-endian byte order; this does not affect the order of DIGEST_0 etc. Field key_swap: If 1, the endianness of each KEY_* register is swapped; default value (0) is big endian representation. Field digest_size: 4-bit one-hot; invalid/unsupported values (including all-zero) are mapped to SHA2_None; with SHA2_None, when HMAC/SHA-2 is triggered to start (via hash_start or hash_continue), it will be blocked from starting and an error is signalled to SW. Field key_length: 6-bit one-hot; for HMAC mode (hmac_en==1), when HMAC is triggered to start while KEY_LENGTH holds Key_None or KEY_LENGTH holds Key_1024 for DIGEST_SIZE=SHA2_256, starting is blocked and an error is signalled to SW; for arbitrary key lengths software should pad zeros to next supported key length according to endianness; note key length cannot exceed block size (1024-bit for SHA-2 384/512, 512-bit for SHA-2 256), and the register value is irrelevant when only SHA-2 (not HMAC) is configured.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies configuration register update behavior and field-specific functions; Informativeness: details when register updates are accepted/discarded, effects of each field on operation and endianness.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CMD register: HMAC command register. Field hash_start: If 1 is written, SHA-2 or HMAC begins operation; CPU must configure relative information first such as digest size, secret key, key length. Field hash_process: If 1 is written, SHA-2 or HMAC calculates the digest or signing based on currently received message. Field hash_stop: When 1 is written, SHA-2 or HMAC will afterwards set the hmac_done interrupt as soon as the current block has been hashed; the hash can then be read from DIGEST_0 to DIGEST_15; together with MSG_LENGTH_LOWER and MSG_LENGTH_UPPER, this forms the information for context saving. Field hash_continue: When 1 is written, SHA-2 or HMAC will continue hashing based on current hash in digest registers and message length, which both have to be restored to switch context.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies command register fields and their effects on HMAC/SHA-2 operation start, process, stop, continue; Informativeness: describes required configuration, digest calculation, interrupt generation on stop, context restore on continue.

ref_atoms.ref_content: STATUS register: HMAC Status register. Field hmac_idle: indicates HMAC idle; when IDLE, the DIGEST and the MSG_LENGTH_LOWER/MSG_LENGTH_UPPER can be written to from SW which enables restoring context (support context switching). Field fifo_full: FIFO full; data written to the FIFO whilst it is full will cause back-pressure on the interconnect.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies status register fields indicating idle condition and FIFO full condition; Informativeness: describes that when idle, DIGEST and MSG_LENGTH can be written for context switching, and that writing full FIFO causes back-pressure.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ERR_CODE register: If an error interrupt occurs, this register contains information of error cause (see prim_sha2_pkg.sv err_code_e enum).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies error code register behavior; Informativeness: indicates register holds error cause when error interrupt occurs.

ref_atoms.ref_content: WIPE_SECRET register: If the CPU writes a value into the register, the value is used to clear internal variables such as the secret key, intermediate hash results, digest and internal message scheduling array. The clear secret operation overwrites the internal variables with the provided 32-bit value. For SHA-2 384/512 that work with 64-bit words, the 32-bit value is duplicated and concatenated to generate the 64-bit value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies the secure wipe register; Informativeness: describes that writing a value clears internal sensitive variables including key, intermediate hash, digest, and for SHA-2 384/512 32-bit value is duplicated.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEY registers (multireg): The registers are allowed to be updated only when the engine is in Idle state. If the engine computes the hash, it discards any attempts to update the secret keys and report an error. The key length determines how many of these registers are relevant for the HMAC operation; order: key[1023:0] = {KEY0, KEY1, ... , KEY31}.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies key register update policy; Informativeness: describes update only allowed when idle, discarding writes and reporting error when hashing.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DIGEST registers (multireg): The digest gets cleared when CFG.sha_en transitions from 1 to 0. When STATUS.hmac_idle is 1, these registers may be written to by software. Outside of this window, writes can cause unpredictable behavior. For SHA-2 256, digest[255:0] = {DIGEST0..DIGEST7} and DIGEST8..DIGEST15 are irrelevant. For SHA-2 384, DIGEST12..DIGEST15 are truncated and irrelevant.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies digest registers behavior; Informativeness: describes cleared when sha_en goes 0, writable by software only when hmac_idle=1, and behavior per digest size.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MSG_LENGTH_LOWER register: Received Message Length calculated by the HMAC in bits [31:0]. Message is byte granularity; lower 3 bits [2:0] are ignored. When STATUS.hmac_idle is 1, this register may be written by software. Outside of this window, writes can cause unpredictable behavior.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies message length lower register behavior; Informativeness: describes writable only when hmac_idle=1, lower 3 bits ignored.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MSG_LENGTH_UPPER register: Received Message Length calculated by the HMAC in bits [63:32]. When STATUS.hmac_idle is 1, this register may be written by software. Outside of this window, writes can cause unpredictable behavior. For SHA-2-256 computations, message length is 64-bit {MSG_LENGTH_UPPER, MSG_LENGTH_LOWER}. For SHA-2 384/512 message length is extended to 128-bit in line with NIST FIPS 180-4 where the upper 64 bits get zero-padded: {32'b0, 32'b0, MSG_LENGTH_UPPER, MSG_LENGTH_LOWER}.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies message length upper register behavior and length extension; Informativeness: describes writable only when hmac_idle=1, and 128-bit extension for SHA-2 384/512.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MSG_FIFO window: Any write to this window will be appended to the FIFO. Only the lower [1:0] bits of the address matter to writes within the window (for correctly dealing with non 32-bit writes).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specificity: specifies the message FIFO window; Informativeness: describes write appends data to FIFO, and only lower 2 address bits matter for non-32-bit writes.

ref_atoms.ref_content:
This error case runs sequences that will cause interrupt bit hmac_err to set. This sequence includes:
- Write msg_fifo or set hash_start when sha is disabled
- Update secret key when hash is in process
- Set hash_start when hash is active
- Write msg before hash_start is set
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to hmac_err interrupt and enumerates specific conditions that trigger it (e.g., writing msg_fifo when sha is disabled, updating secret key during hash).

ref_atoms.ref_content:
This test issues wipe_secret on hmac process datapath. Based on the smoke sequence, this sequence increases the message length, and randomly issues wipe_secret in one of the following scenarios:
- Before entering HMAC secret keys. This scenario represents wiping secrets when HMAC is idle.
- Before issuing HMAC start command. This scenario represents wiping secrets when HMAC entered secret keys.
- Before issuing HMAC process command. This scenario represents wiping secrets when HMAC is streaming in message data.
- Before HMAC finishes hashing process. This scenario represents wiping secrets when HMAC is hashing messages and keys.
**Checks**: The scoreboard will check if digest data are corrupted.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the behavior of wipe_secret signal: issuing wipe_secret during different phases of the HMAC process corrupts the digest data.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Change config registers and secret keys during msg write, make sure access is blocked.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies that modifying config registers and secret keys during msg write is blocked, indicating hardware write protection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify save & restore, which allows SW to switch between different parallel message streams. - This feature is randomly exercised during most of the tests. - When triggered it could go into 3 different scenarios: - Stop and Continue without Saving and Restoring - Save and Restore with same context - Save and Restore with different contexts
Run multiple hmac_long_msg sequences with random on-the-fly reset to ensure that all FSM transitions are exercised.
The message scheduling FIFO is not software accessible but is fed from the 32x32b message FIFO via the HMAC core.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the message scheduling FIFO and explicitly states it is not software accessible.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The HMAC core can forward the message directly from the 32x32b message FIFO if HMAC is not enabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the direct forwarding path from the message FIFO to the SHA-2 engine when HMAC is disabled.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Any write access to the memory-mapped window MSG_FIFO updates the message FIFO. If the FIFO is full, the HMAC block will block any writes leading to back-pressure on the interconnect. Software can read STATUS.fifo_full to avoid writing when the FIFO is full.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes hardware back-pressure behavior on MSG_FIFO writes when FIFO is full and the related STATUS.fifo_full flag.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The logic assumes the input message is little-endian. It converts the byte order of the word right before writing to SHA-2 storage as SHA-2 treats the incoming message as big-endian. If SW wants to convert the message byte order, SW should set CFG.endian_swap to 1.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Refers to CFG.endian_swap and describes the endianness conversion behavior for incoming messages.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The byte order of the digest registers, from DIGEST_0 to DIGEST_15, can be configured with CFG.digest_swap.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Refers to CFG.digest_swap and describes the byte order configuration of the digest registers.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Small writes to MSG_FIFO are coalesced into 32-bit words by the prim_packer logic. While passing writes to the packer logic, the block also counts the number of bytes that are being passed to compute the received message length.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the prim_packer coalescing behavior and the byte counting mechanism used to compute message length.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The SHA-2 padding logic adds an initial '1' bit after the message, then enough '0' padding bits, and finally the message length (64-bit for SHA-256, 128-bit for SHA-384/512). For an empty message in SHA-256, it sends 0x80000000, then 13 times 0x00000000, then the 64-bit zero length. For incomplete words, 0x80 is appended at the appropriate byte location (e.g., 0xXX800000 when message length % 4B == 1).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Provides explicit bit-level padding behavior for complete and incomplete message words, including specific bit patterns.

ref_atoms.ref_content: For SHA-2 256, the SHA-2 engine receives 16 32-bit words from the message FIFO or HMAC core, which get padded into 16 64-bit words (upper 32 bits are all-zero padded), and then begins 64 rounds of hash computation (compression).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the input width extension and round count for SHA-2 256 compression.

ref_atoms.ref_content: For SHA-2 384/512, the SHA-2 engine receives 32 32-bit words from the message FIFO, which get packed into 16 64-bit words, and then begins 80 compression rounds.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the input width extension and round count for SHA-2 384/512 compression.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In each compression round, the function fetches a 64-bit word. The first 16 rounds are fed by the words from the message FIFO or the HMAC core; input for later rounds comes from shuffling the given 512/1024-bit block.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Details the source of data for the first 16 rounds and the shuffled input for later rounds.

ref_atoms.ref_content: During the compression rounds, the SHA-2 engine does not fetch data from the message FIFO.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies that the message FIFO is not accessed during active compression rounds.

ref_atoms.ref_content: After compression at the last round is finished, the resulting hash values are added into the digest registers; the digest is used as initial hash values for the next block compression.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the digest update mechanism involving addition of hash results and reuse for the next block.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The software can push up to 16 (or 32 for SHA-2 384/512) entries to the FIFO for the next hash computation while the current block is being processed. Once the FIFO gets full, the software cannot push more data until the current block is completed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the number of next-block entries that can be preloaded and the blocking behavior when the FIFO is full during compression.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In HMAC, the inner padded key is created with the secret key (zero-padded to block size) XORed with 64{8'h36}. For SHA-256 with 256-bit key: inner_pad_key = {key[255:0], 256'h0} ^ {64{8'h36}}.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Gives the exact formula for inner_pad_key generation including zero-padding and XOR constant.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The message length used in the SHA-2 module for the first HMAC round is calculated by adding the block size to the original message length (to account for the length of inner_pad_key).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the adjustment of message length for the inner key in HMAC.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The outer padded key is created similarly using 0x5c. For SHA-256 with 256-bit key: outer_pad_key = {key[255:0], 256'h0} ^ {64{8'h5c}}.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Gives the exact formula for outer_pad_key generation including zero-padding and XOR constant.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In the second HMAC round, the message length is a fixed 768 bits (512-bit size of outer secret key + 256-bit first round digest size).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the fixed message length for the second HMAC round for SHA-256.

ref_atoms.ref_content: HMAC supports a secret key of length 128, 256, 384, 512, 1024 bits as long as the key length does not exceed the block size of the configured digest. For an arbitrary key length, software should configure the next largest supported key length, hash the key if needed, and concatenate zeros to reach the programmed key size. The position of these zeros depends on CFG.key_swap endianness.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: States the supported key lengths, the requirement to not exceed block size, and the software key-length adaptation procedure involving CFG.key_swap.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The byte order of the key registers is big-endian by default and can be swapped to little-endian by setting CFG.key_swap to 1.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Refers to CFG.key_swap and describes the key register byte order control.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SHA-2 256 takes 80 cycles to complete a 512-bit block.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Provides an exact cycle count for SHA-256 block processing, useful for performance verification.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SHA-2 384/512 takes 96 cycles to complete a 1024-bit block.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Provides an exact cycle count for SHA-384/512 block processing, useful for performance verification.

ref_atoms.ref_content: HMAC SHA-256 introduces an extra 240 cycles (80 for inner key, 80 for outer key, 80 for first round result), resulting in 360 cycles for an empty message.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the additional latency and total cycle count for HMAC processing of an empty message.
